name: New Jersey
note: The Duke of York granted the land between the Hudson and the Delaware to Berkeley and Carteret in 1664 and it was named Nova Caesaria or New Jersey. Label hand-placed west of Newark.

name: East Jersey
note: The Quintipartite Deed of 1676 divided the province; East Jersey (capital Elizabethtown, then Perth Amboy) was reunited with West Jersey as a royal colony in 1702.

name: New Jersey
note: Royal province from 1702 (the proprietors surrendered the government), state from 1776.

name: Bergen County
note: One of the four counties of East Jersey created in 1683; until 1840 it reached south to Bergen Point. Label anchored in today's Hudson County.

name: Hudson County
note: Set off from Bergen County on 22 Feb 1840.

name: Bergen County
note: One of the four counties of East Jersey created in 1683; Passaic County was set off in 1837 and Hudson County in 1840.

name: Essex County
note: One of the four counties of East Jersey created in 1683; lost Acquackanonk to Passaic County in 1837 and its southern half to Union County in 1857.

name: Essex County
note: Today's Union County was the southern half of Essex County from 1683. Label anchored in today's Union County.

name: Union County
note: Set off from Essex County on 19 Mar 1857, the last county created in New Jersey.

name: Passaic County
note: Created on 7 Feb 1837 from Acquackanonk (Essex County) and Pompton, West Milford and part of Saddle River (Bergen County).

name: Westchester County
note: One of the twelve counties created on 1 Nov 1683. The label in the city's table sits in the Bronx until 1874; this one is anchored in the present county.

name: Queens County
note: Today's Nassau County was the eastern part of Queens County (towns of Hempstead, North Hempstead and Oyster Bay) from 1 Nov 1683. Label anchored in today's Nassau County.

name: Nassau County
note: Created on 1 Jan 1899 from the three towns of Queens County left out of Greater New York.

name: Orange County
note: Today's Rockland County was the part of Orange County south of the Highlands from 1 Nov 1683; the county seat was at Tappan. Label anchored in today's Rockland County.

name: Rockland County
note: Set off from Orange County on 23 Feb 1798.

name: The Palisades
note: Basalt cliffs along the Hudson from Jersey City to Nyack. No naming date found; start is nominal. Label hand-placed on the cliff above Englewood Cliffs.

name: Hackensack Meadows
note: Tidal marsh and white-cedar swamp of the lower Hackensack. Start is nominal; the label hands over when the state created the Hackensack Meadowlands Development Commission in 1969. Shared by Bergen and Hudson counties.

name: The Meadowlands
note: Name in general use after the Hackensack Meadowlands Development Commission of 1969 (estimated as the hand-over year). Shared by Bergen and Hudson counties.

name: Achter Kol
note: Dutch name ("behind the ridge") for Newark Bay and the country behind Bergen Neck. Start is nominal (the first years of New Netherland); the English name follows the founding of Newark.

name: Newark Bay
note: Named for the town founded on the Passaic in 1666; start is nominal. Shared by Hudson, Essex and Union counties.

name: Hackensack River
note: Named for the Hackensack band of the Lenape; start is nominal. Label at New Bridge.

name: Passaic River
note: From the Lenape pahsayek, valley; start is nominal. Label on the reach between Paterson and Passaic.

name: Watchung Mountains
note: Three basalt ridges west of Newark, from the Lenape wach unks, high hills; First Mountain was long called Orange Mountain. Start is nominal. Shared by Essex, Union and Passaic counties.

name: Ramapo Mountains
note: Part of the Highlands along the New Jersey - New York line; start is nominal. Shared by Bergen, Passaic and Rockland counties.

name: Long Pond
note: Colonial name of the lake on the state line, dammed and enlarged for the Long Pond ironworks (1766) and the Morris Canal (1830s). Start is nominal; the renaming to Greenwood Lake is dated to about 1860, estimated.

name: Greenwood Lake
note: Resort-era name of Long Pond; year estimated. Shared by Passaic County and Orange County, New York.

name: Great Falls
note: The 23 m falls of the Passaic, called Totowa Falls or Passaic Falls in colonial accounts; start is nominal. The Society for Establishing Useful Manufactures built its raceways here from 1792.

name: Tappan Zee
note: Dutch name (zee = sea) for the widest reach of the Hudson, after the Tappan people; start is nominal. Shared by Rockland and Westchester counties.

name: Haverstraw Bay
note: From the Dutch haverstroo, oat straw, on maps from 1616; start is nominal. Shared by Rockland and Westchester counties.

name: Hudson Highlands
note: The river's gorge through the Appalachians north of Peekskill and Stony Point; start is nominal. Shared by Westchester, Rockland, Putnam and Orange counties.

name: Pavonia
note: Patroonship of Michiel Pauw, bought from the Lenape in 1630; the company took it back in 1637. The settlements were destroyed in Kieft's War (1643) and the Peach War (1655); Stuyvesant repurchased the land in 1658 (end year).

name: Hopoghan Hackingh
note: Lenape name, "land of the tobacco pipe", for the serpentine bluff of Castle Point. End year: the sale to Michiel Pauw, 1630.

name: Hoebuck
note: Dutch form of the name; Aert van Putten leased the land in 1643 and built the first brewery; the Bayard family estate until it was confiscated and sold to John Stevens in 1784.

name: Hoboken
note: John Stevens bought the island in 1784 and laid out the town in 1804; township 1849.

name: Hoboken
note: Incorporated as a city on 28 Mar 1855.

name: Aressick
note: Lenape name of the sandy point opposite Manhattan, an island at high tide. End year: the grant to Michael Paulez, 1638.

name: Paulus Hook
note: Granted in 1638 to Michael Paulez (Paulusen), Pauw's agent, who kept an occasional ferry and traded with the Lenape; ferry to New York from 1764, fort stormed by Henry Lee in 1779. Year 1804 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Jersey
note: The Associates of the Jersey Company laid out the Town of Jersey on Paulus Hook in 1804; City of Jersey 1820.

name: Jersey City
note: Reincorporated as Jersey City on 22 Feb 1838; absorbed Van Vorst (1851), Hudson City and Bergen (1870) and Greenville (1873). Label kept at Paulus Hook, the first town.

name: Paulus Hook
note: The old town as a district of Jersey City. Hand-placed 500 m west of the city label. Year 1838 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Ahasimus
note: Lenape place on the cove north of Paulus Hook. End year: the homestead built in 1634 by Pauw's superintendent, Cornelis van Vorst. Hand-placed at Harsimus Cove.

name: Harsimus
note: Homestead of Cornelis van Vorst, Pauw's superintendent, from 1634; the West India Company's farm, later the Duke's Farm. Year 1841 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Van Vorst
note: Township formed in 1841 from Bergen Township; annexed by Jersey City in 1851.

name: Harsimus
note: District of Jersey City (Harsimus Cove, Hamilton Park, Van Vorst Park). Year 1851 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Gemoenepaen
note: First house of Pavonia built here in 1634 for Jan Evertsen Bout; the Lenape camp nearby was attacked on 25 Feb 1643; village laid out again in 1660. Dutch spelling of a Lenape name. Year 1664 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Communipaw
note: English spelling. Name switch dated to the English takeover of 1664 (nominal). Village of Bergen Township until Bergen joined Jersey City in 1870.

name: Communipaw
note: District of Jersey City; its shore was filled for the Central Railroad of New Jersey terminal (1864-1889), now Liberty State Park.

name: Bergen
note: Palisaded village laid out in 1660 by order of Stuyvesant, the first permanent town in New Jersey; own court 1661; Town of Bergen 1855, City of Bergen 1868, joined Jersey City in 1870. Year 1870 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Bergen Square
note: The square of the 1660 village, at Bergen Avenue and Academy Street, as a district of Jersey City. Year 1870 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Hudson City
note: Town of Hudson 1852, Hudson City 1855, on the ridge north of Bergen; joined Jersey City in 1870. Hand-placed on Central Avenue.

name: The Heights
note: The former Hudson City as a district of Jersey City. Year 1870 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Greenville
note: Township set off from Bergen in 1863; annexed by Jersey City in 1873.

name: Greenville
note: District of Jersey City.

name: Journal Square
note: Square created over the Hudson Tubes cut and named in 1923 for the Jersey Journal.

name: Newport
note: Built from 1986 on the former Erie Railroad yards at Pavonia.

name: Black Tom
note: Island in the bay joined to the shore by a railroad causeway and fill about 1880 (estimated) for the Lehigh Valley's munitions piers; blown up by German agents on 30 Jul 1916. Now part of Liberty State Park.

name: Constable Hook
note: Granted in 1646 to Jacob Jacobsen Roy, the chief gunner (konstapel) of Fort Amsterdam.

name: Bergen Point
note: Southern tip of Bergen Neck on the Kill Van Kull; start is nominal.

name: Bayonne
note: Township formed in 1861 from Bergen Township (Bergen Point, Centreville, Pamrapo, Saltersville).

name: Bayonne
note: Incorporated as a city on 10 Mar 1869.

name: New Barbadoes Neck
note: Neck between the Hackensack and the Passaic granted in 1668 to William Sandford of Barbados. End year estimated (the name went out of use). Hand-placed in Kearny.

name: Harrison
note: Township set off from Lodi Township when Hudson County was created in 1840; town 1869.

name: Kearny
note: Township set off from Harrison in 1867 and named for General Philip Kearny, whose house stood here; town 1898. Label hand-placed on Kearny Avenue at the town hall.

name: East Newark
note: Incorporated in 1895 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Snake Hill
note: Diabase knob in the meadows (Slangenbergh, officially Laurel Hill since 1926), the county's almshouse and asylum site 1863-1962; half quarried away. Start is nominal.

name: Secaucus
note: Borough set off from North Bergen in 1900, town 1917; farms on the upland island in the meadows from the 1660s. Label hand-placed at the Plaza on Paterson Plank Road.

name: North Bergen
note: Township formed in 1843 from the northern part of Bergen Township.

name: Weehawken
note: Township formed in 1859 from Hoboken and North Bergen. The name (Awiehawken) is Lenape; the duelling ground under the cliff was used from 1798 to 1845 (Hamilton and Burr, 1804).

name: Guttenberg
note: Laid out by a German land association and incorporated as a town within North Bergen in 1859.

name: West Hoboken
note: Township 1861, town 1884; merged with Union Hill on 1 Jun 1925. Hand-placed on Summit Avenue.

name: Union Hill
note: Town set off from Union Township in 1864; merged with West Hoboken on 1 Jun 1925. Hand-placed near 32nd Street.

name: Union City
note: Created on 1 Jun 1925 by the merger of West Hoboken and Union Hill.

name: West New York
note: Incorporated as a town in 1898, replacing Union Township.

name: Achkinheshacky
note: Chief village of the Hackensack band of the Lenape under the sachem Oratam, between Overpeck Creek and the Hackensack. Location approximate. End year estimated: Oratam died about 1667-69 and the land had been sold.

name: Achter Col
note: Colony planted in 1641 by Myndert Myndertsen van der Horst on the Hackensack near today's Bogota, burnt in Kieft's War in 1643. Location approximate.

name: New Barbadoes
note: Township from 1693 (in Bergen County from 1710) whose village was Hackensack; renamed the City of Hackensack in 1921. Hand-placed south-west of the green so that the two labels do not collide. Year 1693 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Hackensack
note: The Dutch church on the Green dates from 1696 and the county courts moved here in 1710; officially New Barbadoes Township until 1921. Burnt by the British in 1780. Label at the court house on the Green.

name: English Neighborhood
note: Samuel Edsall bought the land between Overpeck Creek and the Hudson in 1668 and it soon became known as the English Neighborhood; it became Ridgefield Township in 1871.

name: Ridgefield
note: Ridgefield Township was formed from Hackensack Township in 1871; the borough dates from 1892. Year 1871 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Fort Lee
note: Fort Constitution, built in July 1776 on the Palisades, was renamed for General Charles Lee that autumn and abandoned on 20 Nov 1776; the village kept the name. Borough 1904.

name: Liberty Pole
note: Tavern and crossroads named for the pole raised at the repeal of the Stamp Act, 1766 (estimated as the start).

name: Englewood
note: Named in 1859 when the Northern Railroad of New Jersey opened; township 1871, city 1899.

name: Godwinville
note: Village of Franklin Township named in 1829 for the Revolutionary officer Abraham Godwin. Year 1829 / 1866 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Ridgewood
note: Name adopted in 1866; township 1876, village 1894. Year 1866 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Paramus
note: From the Lenape Perampsepus. The Paramus Reformed congregation dates from 1725 (its church stands just over the line in Ridgewood); borough 1922. Year 1725 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Boiling Springs
note: Earlier name of the neighbourhood, from a spring; start estimated.

name: Rutherford
note: Named for John Rutherfurd; borough formed from Union Township in 1881.

name: Union
note: Union Township was created in 1852 from the part of Harrison Township, Hudson County, returned to Bergen County.

name: Lyndhurst
note: Union Township was renamed Lyndhurst in 1917.

name: Carlstadt
note: Founded in 1851 by a German land association led by Carl Klein; borough 1894. Year 1851 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: East Paterson
note: Borough formed from Saddle River Township in 1916.

name: Elmwood Park
note: East Paterson was renamed Elmwood Park on 1 Jan 1973.

name: Delford
note: Borough of 1894, named from Oradell and New Milford.

name: Oradell
note: Delford was renamed Oradell in 1920.

name: Schraalenburgh
note: Dutch farming neighbourhood ("barren ridge"); its church was organised in 1724 (estimated as the start). Borough 1894.

name: Dumont
note: Schraalenburgh was renamed in 1898 for its first mayor, Dumont Clarke.

name: New Bridge
note: A road was surveyed in 1744 to the narrows of the Hackensack where the "New Bridge" was built; Washington's army crossed it in the retreat of 20 Nov 1776. Year 1894 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Riverside
note: Borough of 1894.

name: River Edge
note: Riverside was renamed River Edge in 1930.

name: Etna
note: Borough of 1903 (the neighbourhood was Kinderkamack).

name: Emerson
note: Etna was renamed in 1909 for Ralph Waldo Emerson.

name: Undercliff
note: Borough of 1894 under the Palisades.

name: Edgewater
note: Undercliff was renamed Edgewater in 1899.

name: Closter
note: Farms from 1704 (the Vervalen family); borough 1904. Year 1704 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Mahwah
note: From the Lenape mawewi, meeting place; Blandina Bayard's trading post of about 1700. The township, Hohokus Township from 1849, took the name in 1944. Label hand-placed at the railroad station.

name: Garfield
note: East Passaic was renamed in 1881 for President Garfield; borough 1898, city 1917.

name: Lodi
note: Lodi Township was formed in 1825 from New Barbadoes; the borough dates from 1894. Year 1825 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Radburn
note: "Town for the motor age" planned by Clarence Stein and Henry Wright; first families moved in in 1929.

name: Allendale
note: Incorporated in 1894 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Alpine
note: Incorporated in 1903 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start. Label hand-placed at the borough hall on Closter Dock Road.

name: Bergenfield
note: Incorporated in 1894 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Bogota
note: Incorporated in 1894 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Cliffside Park
note: Incorporated in 1895 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Cresskill
note: Incorporated as a borough in 1894 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Demarest
note: Incorporated in 1903 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: East Rutherford
note: Boiling Springs Township (1889) became the borough of East Rutherford in 1894. Label hand-placed at the borough hall.

name: Englewood Cliffs
note: Incorporated in 1895 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start. Label hand-placed on Sylvan Avenue.

name: Fair Lawn
note: Incorporated as a borough in 1924 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Fairview
note: Incorporated in 1894 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Franklin Lakes
note: Incorporated in 1922 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Glen Rock
note: Incorporated in 1894 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Harrington Park
note: Incorporated in 1904 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Hasbrouck Heights
note: Incorporated in 1894 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Haworth
note: Incorporated in 1904 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Hillsdale
note: Incorporated as a borough in 1923 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Ho-Ho-Kus
note: Incorporated as a borough in 1908 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Leonia
note: Incorporated in 1894 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Little Ferry
note: Incorporated in 1894 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Maywood
note: Incorporated as a borough in 1894 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Midland Park
note: Incorporated as a borough in 1894 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Montvale
note: Incorporated as a borough in 1894 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Moonachie
note: Incorporated as a borough in 1910 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: New Milford
note: Incorporated as a borough in 1922 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: North Arlington
note: Incorporated as a borough in 1896 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Northvale
note: Incorporated in 1916 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Norwood
note: Incorporated in 1905 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start. Label hand-placed on Broadway at the borough hall.

name: Oakland
note: Incorporated as a borough in 1902 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Old Tappan
note: Incorporated as a borough in 1894 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Palisades Park
note: Incorporated in 1899 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Park Ridge
note: Incorporated in 1894 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Ramsey
note: Incorporated as a borough in 1908 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Ridgefield Park
note: Incorporated in 1892 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: River Vale
note: Incorporated as a township in 1906 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Rochelle Park
note: Midland Township, formed in 1871, was renamed Rochelle Park in 1929.

name: Rockleigh
note: Incorporated as a borough in 1923 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Saddle Brook
note: Saddle River Township, formed in 1716, was renamed Saddle Brook in 1955.

name: Saddle River
note: Incorporated as a borough in 1894 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: South Hackensack
note: What was left of Lodi Township was renamed South Hackensack in 1935.

name: Teaneck
note: Incorporated in 1895 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Tenafly
note: Incorporated as a borough in 1894 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Teterboro
note: Incorporated in 1917 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Upper Saddle River
note: Incorporated in 1894 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Waldwick
note: Incorporated in 1919 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Wallington
note: Borough created on 2 Jan 1895 from Lodi and Saddle River townships.

name: Washington Township
note: Incorporated in 1840 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Westwood
note: Incorporated as a borough in 1894 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Wood-Ridge
note: Incorporated as a borough in 1894 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Woodcliff Lake
note: Incorporated in 1894 as the borough of Woodcliff; Woodcliff Lake since 1910.

name: Wyckoff
note: Franklin Township was renamed Wyckoff in 1926; the name of the neighbourhood is far older.

name: Newark
note: Founded in May 1666 by Puritans from the New Haven Colony led by Robert Treat, who bought the land from the Hackensack Lenape; township 1693. Label at Broad and Market streets, the crossing of the 1666 town plan.

name: Newark
note: Incorporated as a city in 1836; absorbed Clinton Township (1902) and Vailsburg (1905).

name: Ironbound
note: The Down Neck district east of Penn Station, ringed by railroads; the name is dated to about 1900, estimated.

name: Forest Hill
note: Residential district laid out beside Branch Brook Park from the 1890s; year estimated.

name: Roseville
note: District around the Morris and Essex Railroad's Roseville station; year estimated.

name: Woodside
note: Woodside Township (1869) was divided between Newark and Belleville in 1871.

name: Vailsburg
note: Borough set off from South Orange Township in 1894; annexed by Newark on 1 Jan 1905.

name: Vailsburg
note: District of Newark since the annexation of 1905.

name: Weequahic
note: District built up in the 1920s beside Weequahic Park; year estimated. The Lenape name marked the boundary creek between the Hackensack and Raritan bands.

name: Newark Mountains
note: The western part of the Newark grant, settled from about 1678 (estimated); the Mountain Society church was organised in 1719.

name: Orange
note: The name Orange was adopted in 1780; township 1806, town 1860, city 1872.

name: East Orange
note: Township set off from Orange in 1863; city 1899.

name: West Orange
note: Fairmount Township (1862) was enlarged and renamed West Orange in 1863; town 1900. Label hand-placed on Main Street at the town hall.

name: South Orange
note: South Orange Township was set off from Clinton and Orange in 1861; the village dates from 1869.

name: Maplewood
note: The Morris and Essex Railroad named its station Maplewood about 1860 (estimated); the village was Jefferson Village. South Orange Township took the name in 1922.

name: Camptown
note: Village on the Elizabeth River settled from about 1692; start estimated.

name: Irvington
note: Camptown was renamed in 1852 for Washington Irving; village 1874, town 1898. Year 1852 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Wardsesson
note: Northern ward of Newark township (the name survives as Watsessing); start estimated.

name: Bloomfield
note: The Presbyterian Society of Bloomfield, formed in 1794, was named for General Joseph Bloomfield (the naming is often dated 1796); its church stands on the Green. Township 1812.

name: Cranetown
note: Settled in 1694 by Azariah Crane of Newark. Year 1694 / 1812 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: West Bloomfield
note: Cranetown became the western part of Bloomfield Township in 1812. Year 1812 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Montclair
note: The name Montclair was adopted in 1860; township set off from Bloomfield in 1868.

name: Second River
note: Dutch settlement at the mouth of the Second River; its Reformed church dates from 1697. Start estimated.

name: Belleville
note: Second River was renamed Belleville in 1797; township 1839.

name: Franklin
note: Franklin Township was set off from Belleville in 1874.

name: Nutley
note: Franklin was renamed Nutley in 1902, after an estate on the Passaic.

name: Horseneck
note: Tract west of the mountains bought from the Lenape in 1702; scene of the land riots of the 1740s. Year 1702 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Caldwell
note: Caldwell Township was formed in 1798 and named for the Reverend James Caldwell; the borough dates from 1892. Year 1798 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Livingston
note: Township formed in 1813 and named for Governor William Livingston.

name: Millburn
note: Township formed in 1857 from the part of Springfield left in Essex County.

name: Short Hills
note: Planned suburb begun by Stewart Hartshorn in 1877. Year 1877 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Llewellyn Park
note: Residential park laid out from 1857 by Llewellyn Haskell, the first planned garden suburb in the country.

name: Glen Ridge
note: Incorporated in 1895 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Verona
note: Incorporated in 1907 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Cedar Grove
note: Verona Township, formed in 1892, was renamed Cedar Grove in 1908.

name: Essex Fells
note: Incorporated as a borough in 1902 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: North Caldwell
note: Incorporated in 1898 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: West Caldwell
note: Incorporated as a borough in 1904 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Roseland
note: Incorporated as a borough in 1908 (year read from the cited article); the first use of the name was not researched - nominal start.

name: Fairfield
note: Caldwell Township, formed in 1798, was renamed Fairfield in 1963.

name: Elizabethtown
note: First English settlement in New Jersey: land bought from the Lenape on 28 Oct 1664 by the Elizabethtown Associates; capital of the province until 1686. Label at the Presbyterian church of 1664 on Broad Street.

name: Elizabeth
note: Incorporated as the City of Elizabeth in 1855; county seat of Union County from 1857.

name: Elizabethport
note: Hand-placed. Port on the Arthur Kill laid out about 1835 (estimated), terminus of the Elizabethtown and Somerville Railroad (1839) and of the Singer works (1873).

name: Connecticut Farms
note: Settled in 1667 by families from Connecticut; burnt by the British on 7 Jun 1780. Year 1667 / 1808 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Union
note: Union Township was set off from Elizabeth in 1808.

name: Springfield
note: Settled about 1717 (estimated); township 1793. The British advance on Morristown was stopped here on 23 Jun 1780.

name: Westfield
note: The "West Fields" of Elizabethtown, settled about 1720; township 1794, town 1903.

name: Scotch Plains
note: Settled in 1684 by Scottish Quakers and Presbyterians; the township (Fanwood Township from 1877) took the name in 1917.

name: Plainfield
note: Quakers settled the plain in 1684; the Friends moved their meeting house here in 1788; township 1847, city 1869.

name: Spanktown
note: Colonial name of the village on the Rahway River; start estimated. Skirmish of 5 Jan 1777.

name: Rahway
note: Rahway Township was formed in 1804; city 1858. Year 1804 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Turkey
note: Village of the upper Passaic valley (Turkey Town); its Presbyterian church was organised in 1737. End year estimated.

name: New Providence
note: Renamed New Providence, by tradition after the church gallery fell in 1759 without loss of life (other accounts give 1778) - year estimated; township 1809, borough 1899.

name: New Orange
note: Industrial town promoted from 1894 by the New Orange Industrial Association. Year 1894 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Kenilworth

name: Marsapeague
note: Band of the south shore whose palisaded fort stood on Fort Neck. Their sachem Tackapausha sold much of the land to the settlers of Oyster Bay and Hempstead by 1658 (estimated end).

name: Meroke
note: Band of the south shore between the Rockaways and Massapequa (Merikoke). End year: the Hempstead purchase of 1643. Location approximate.

name: Matinecock
note: People of the north shore from Flushing to the Nissequogue; the necks around Musketa Cove and Oyster Bay were theirs. Location approximate (Glen Cove); end year estimated (the Musketa Cove purchase of 1667-68).

name: Hempstead Plains
note: Sixty thousand acres of natural prairie, the town of Hempstead's common pasture from 1644 and the cradle of American aviation; a few hectares survive.

name: Hempstead Harbor
note: Bay of the Sound between Cow Neck and Glen Cove; start is nominal.

name: Cow Bay
note: Bay west of Cow Neck (the town of Hempstead fenced the neck as a cattle pasture in the 1670s); start is nominal.

name: Manhasset Bay
note: Cow Bay was renamed Manhasset Bay in 1907.

name: Cow Neck
note: Peninsula between Manhasset Bay and Hempstead Harbor, fenced as the common cattle pasture of Hempstead in the 1670s; start estimated. Also Manhasset Neck.

name: Great Neck
note: Madnan's Neck of the first settlers; called Great Neck by the 1670s (estimated).

name: Oyster Bay Harbor
note: Named by the Dutch (Oester Baai) by 1639 for its shellfish. Year 1639 not found in the cited article: estimated.

name: Jones Beach
note: Barrier beach named for Major Thomas Jones, who settled at Fort Neck in 1696 and had a whaling station on the beach about 1700; the state park opened in 1929.

name: South Oyster Bay
note: Lagoon behind Jones Beach; start is nominal.

name: Success Pond
note: Kettle pond on the moraine (Sucut); start is nominal.

name: Lake Success
note: The pond is called Lake Success since the village of that name was incorporated; year estimated.

name: Roosevelt Field
note: The Hempstead Plains Aerodrome (1911) was named in 1919 for Quentin Roosevelt; Lindbergh took off for Paris here on 20 May 1927. Closed in 1951; the shopping mall opened in 1956.

name: Mitchel Field
note: Army airfield on the Hempstead Plains named in 1918 for Mayor John Purroy Mitchel; closed in 1961.
